Align development and coverage tooling

Run pretest before coverage and benchmarks so both commands have their required fixtures and generated bindings. Use c8 for text and HTML coverage reports, remove the duplicate Node.js report, and exclude all generated bindings.

Convert development scripts to .mjs modules and check HTTP status before saving fixtures. Keep the shared fixture list in its own module so NO_UPDATE skips downloads without exiting the test process.

Fix WPT exception assertions so unexpected error types fail while errors from different realms remain supported; previously, the expected error name was treated only as an assertion message. Use node:assert/strict with the short assertion names throughout the Node.js tests.

Make unexpected benchmark task errors fail the command. Name the live-viewer build command build:live-viewer and use Node.js LTS for its deployment workflow.

Declare the CommonJS package type and lint .mjs files with Node.js globals that exclude CommonJS-only bindings. Align ESLint configuration structure, npm script ordering, Git ignore patterns, and LF line endings with the other jsdom projects. Preserve browser globals for the live viewer and add the shared EditorConfig settings.

Use ci.yml with the CI workflow name, multiline YAML lists, consistent job and step names, and read-only repository permissions. Enforce dependency engines in workflow installations and explicitly test Node.js 26.0.0 alongside the existing minimum versions.

Update development dependencies, including ESLint config 6.1.0, and regenerate the lockfile.
